title: The Dark Side of Mobile App Adoption: Examining the Impact on Customers' Multichannel Purchase
design_notes: Hotel group data, Jan 2011 to Feb 2015, 60,000 customers in six app-adoption cohorts (adoption months spread Aug 2011 to Feb 2015); all customers eventually adopt before Feb 2015. Main analysis (Eq. 1, Table 2) builds ten treatment-control cohort pairs (e.g., Cohort 1 vs. Cohorts 3-6) and estimates a standard two-period DID on pre/post averages (six months before and after adoption, adoption month dropped) with time-varying reservation controls x_it and demographics, plus Heckman (inverse Mills ratio) and 1:1 propensity-score matching variants. Robustness: multiperiod panel DID per pair (Eq. 4) with month dummies, customer FE, controls and three instruments; Eq. 5 adds a time trend.
eligible_reason: Each estimate compares one treated cohort with not-yet-adopters over a single adoption date (cohort-pair 2x2, not a pooled staggered TWFE); includes time-varying controls, Heckman correction, matching, and IV in the panel version; main estimate uses pre/post-collapsed two-period data.
screener_notes: Proprietary customer-level reservation and app-usage data from a hotel group; no package or data statement. Borderline in the sense that the underlying data are staggered across six cohorts and one could pool them in a TWFE, but the paper never reports such a specification, so nothing qualifies for the main-text rule.
screened_from: article text only (no package_dir or regressions file in batch_t2_004)
